subject: Proposed DPA language: locality tiers, retention exceptions, and deletion evidence
messages:
From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@aurum.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@eclipseapps.com>
Date: 2028-07-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA: locality tiers + retention exceptions questions

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the draft DPA. A few items came up on our side while reviewing retention and residency clauses:

- We need clarity on how "locality tiers" are defined (regional vs country-level). Can Redwood commit to country-level residency for PII in the EU in the redline?
- Backups / snapshot copies: what is the maximum backup retention window, and do backups fall under the same erase-window as primary data?
- Deletion evidence: our compliance folks want a mechanism to receive certification that data was erased from backups and caches (not just primary stores). Do you provide a standard report or certificate?

Cornerstone asks: if we request customer data erasure, what is the practical end-to-end timeline (including any onshore transfer or legal hold handling)?

Attached is our standard DPA appendix for reference (we'll follow with a marked-up version). Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Elena
Elena Novak
Head of Security & Privacy, Aurum Health
elena.novak@aurum.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@aurum.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: locality tiers + retention exceptions questions

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then proposed redline approach below.

Summary answers:
- Locality tiers: we can offer country-level residency for EU PII for production datasets when customers choose the EU residency option; we do not automatically geo-replicate outside the selected geozone.
- Backups: backups are retained by default for up to 30 days in active snapshot rotation; cold snapshots (for restore/DR) are kept for an additional 60 days unless a customer requests a shorter TTL.
- Deletion evidence: we can provide a deletion certificate that includes a record of primary-store erasure and a backup snapshot purge log; ephemeral cache items are logged separately.

Proposed negotiation posture (what we can commit in the DPA):
1) Country-level residency option: add a clause letting customers opt into country-level residency where available; Redwood will maintain primary copies in the selected country/region, with metadata for routing preserved.
2) Backup TTL: commit to a maximum backup snapshot retention of 90 days for standard accounts (with the option for customers to shorten that TTL).
3) Deletion timeline: standard certified deletion within 45 days of a validated request; for exceptional legal holds we will provide notice and extend timelines with defined carveouts.
4) Deletion evidence package: provide certification (PDF) plus a log extract showing snapshot IDs and purge actions; include a one-time SOC-style attestation for annual audits.

I'm attaching a draft redline and our deletion playbook excerpt for your review. Internal folks, please see comments below from Karthik and Marcus.

Next step: Elena, if the 45-day certificate timeline and 90-day snapshot cap look acceptable, we can send a tagged redline in-track.

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Elena Novak <elena.novak@aurum.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-04T11:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: locality tiers + retention exceptions questions

Elena / Priya —

Quick technical clarifications and an operator playbook snippet so expectations align:

- Country-level residency: where we provide country-level tenancy we pin primary replicas to that region. However, telemetry/metrics and anonymized runtime traces may still be routed to central observability clusters unless explicitly excluded — we can add language to note telemetry-only flows are non-PII and excluded.

- Backup retention: practical flow is primary snapshot -> cold snapshot (tagged) -> archive window. Purging a snapshot is an asynchronous operation:
  * Request received -> mark snapshots for purge (within 24h)
  * Purge job executes (typically within 72h per replica)
  * Final ledger entry generated once all replicas confirm purge (can take up to the DPA committed window)

- Cache/ephemeral: KV caches are ephemeral; we run a TTL-based eviction. For deletion requests we flush relevant prefixes and return a cache purge token in the evidence package.

Operator playbook excerpt (for deletion request):
1) Validate identity & scope
2) Suspend live replication for affected tenant
3) Initiate primary-data erasure tasks and confirm returns
4) Mark and queue snapshots for purge; log snapshot IDs
5) Flush KV cache prefixes and record purge token
6) Run verification job across replicas and generate deletion certificate

This flow typically completes sooner than the advertised window for most simple scopes; the 45-day window covers edge cases (large snapshot counts, cross-region restore dependencies).

-Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@aurum.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@eclipseapps.com>, legal@aurum.ai
Date: 2028-07-04T13:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: locality tiers + retention exceptions questions

Thanks Priya — that helps. A few follow-ups from our side after internal review:

1) Our privacy team wants the backup cap to be contractual at 60 days rather than 90. They argue their data lifecycle policy requires shorter retention for certain datasets. Would Redwood consider 60 days as a standard for EU PII?
2) For deletion evidence, could you include a machine-readable JSON payload (in addition to the PDF certificate) that includes snapshot IDs, purge timestamps, and cache purge tokens — our tooling will ingest that directly.
3) We also want a limited carveout for lawful requests from EU authorities; can you add a notification window (e.g., Redwood will notify the customer within 72 hours if compelled to disclose)?

I've attached a marked-up appendix with proposed edits. If we can't reach an agreement on retention cap, this will likely need escalation to procurement and legal.

-elena

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@aurum.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-04T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: locality tiers + retention exceptions questions

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. From a legal standpoint we're prepared to offer the following compromise to finalize the redline without escalation:

- Backup retention cap: 60 days for EU PII when customer elects the EU residency addendum; by default accounts remain at 90 days unless the customer signs the residency addendum.
- Deletion evidence: Redwood will provide both a human-readable deletion certificate (PDF) and a JSON evidence payload containing snapshot IDs, purge timestamps, and cache purge tokens. We'll include a data dictionary for the JSON schema.
- Lawful access / compelled disclosure: Redwood will provide notification to the customer within 72 hours unless prohibited by law; where prohibited, Redwood will provide notice as soon as legally permitted.
- Certified deletion timeline: confirm certified deletion within 45 days; for large-scale restores or third-party escrow backups that extend this timeline we will provide interim status updates every 7 days.

If you accept, we'll incorporate these items into a final DPA redline (attached) and circulate for signature. Marcus and Karthik — please confirm the operator playbook can produce the JSON payload fields Olga requests (snapshot_id, purge_ts, cache_purge_token, verification_hash).

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@aurum.ai>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-04T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: locality tiers + retention exceptions questions

Elena —

Thanks — glad we found common ground. Next steps we propose:

1) Redwood sends the updated DPA redline (incorporating the 60-day EU backup cap for residency addendum, JSON evidence payload, and 72-hour notification commitment) by end of day tomorrow. (Attached: Aurum_DPA_redline_v3.docx)
2) We will also share deletion-evidence-playbook.pdf and backup-snapshot-matrix.xlsx for your technical team's ingestion tests.
3) If Aurum signs the residency addendum we will switch the default snapshot TTL for your account to 60 days on activation.

We'll await confirmation from Elena/a legal to proceed to signature. Happy to schedule a short call to walk through the JSON schema if helpful.

Thanks all,
Priya
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com
